title: A scan says how many films it could not store
description: A scan that stores none of its films reports success; an operator sees no sign that films failed to probe or store.
acceptanceCriteria: With a store wrapper that fails every read of 2 of 5 new films in one scan, the other 3 are stored as exactly 3 items a viewer can list, and the 2 have no item
That scan's closing log line names the library and says 2 films failed, and each of the 2 has its own log line with its key and the error

After that scan, for that library's ID: the gauge jellyscale_scan_last_failed_films is 2, jellyscale_scan_last_success is 0, and jellyscale_scan_last_timestamp_seconds and jellyscale_scan_last_duration_seconds are that scan's
A scan in which all 5 of 5 films fail, in a library with nothing stored, says 5 failed in the log line and the gauge and sets jellyscale_scan_last_success to 0
The count is of one scan: a second scan while the same 2 still fail says 2 again (not 0, not 4) and jellyscale_scan_last_success stays 0
The next scan after the wrapper stops failing, with no file changed, stores the 2 (5 items in all), sets jellyscale_scan_last_success to 1 and the gauge to 0, and its log line says 0 failed
A film that was probed but whose write to Postgres failed is counted the same as one whose probe failed
A file that is not a film (junk bytes under a video name) counts as 1 failed at every scan until it is replaced by a film or removed, and the scan after that is clean
An episode file skipped for having no season and episode number is not counted: a scan with one and no failure reports 0 failed and success 1
A stored film whose file is replaced by one that cannot be probed is counted as failed and keeps its item, visible, with its ID and watch state, at every scan, also after missingGrace
With the default maxLostShare (0.2), 2 of 5 stored films failing that way do not fail the scan on the mass-loss guard, and nothing is hidden or removed
A scan with failed films still does the rest of its work: a stored film whose file is gone from the store in that same scan is hidden as in a clean scan
With two libraries scanned by one process, 2 failed films in one leave the other's gauge at 0 and its jellyscale_scan_last_success at 1
A scan another replica holds the lock for, or one cut short by shutdown, leaves the gauge and jellyscale_scan_last_success of the library as they were
docs/running.md names the gauge in its metrics table and says jellyscale_scan_last_success is 0 when any film could not be stored
